key_insight: V-Retrver adds an agentic, evidence-driven verification loop to multimodal retrieval: the model actively extracts and checks fine-grained visual evidence during reasoning, reducing speculative Chain-of-Thought and improving reranking reliability.
problem_solved: Existing MLLM-based retrieval methods rely on static visual encodings and language-only CoT, which can produce speculative or incorrect reranking in visually ambiguous cases; V-Retrver enables active visual verification to ground decisions in concrete evidence.
method: Agentic evidence acquisition: the system selects image regions or formulates focused visual queries to extract fine-grained evidence instead of using only global/static encodings.
Iterative evidence-driven reasoning: integrate retrieved visual evidence into an agentic Chain-of-Thought loop that verifies, refines, or rejects hypotheses about candidate matches.
Evidence-aware reranking: use the outcome of verification steps to score and rerank retrieval candidates, prioritizing those supported by concrete visual evidence.
impact: Grounding multimodal retrieval in verifiable visual evidence yields more reliable, interpretable reranking—beneficial for search, VQA, and any vision–language application that needs precise, trustworthy retrieval.

paper_title: V-Retrver: Evidence-Driven Agentic Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval
paper_authors: Dongyang Chen, Chaoyang Wang, Dezhao SU, Xi Xiao, Zeyu Zhang
